message.content:
Based on my search, here's a comprehensive guide to understanding pregnancy test results:

## Types of Pregnancy Tests

There are two main types of pregnancy tests:
- **Urine tests**: Home pregnancy tests you can buy at drugstores
- **Blood tests**: Done at a doctor's office, more sensitive and can measure exact hCG levels

## How to Read Results

### Standard Line Tests
| Result | What You See | Meaning |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| **Positive** | Two lines (Control + Test) | Pregnant - even a faint test line means positive |
| **Negative** | One line (Control only) | Not pregnant |
| **Invalid** | No lines, or only Test line | Test didn't work properly - retake |

### Digital Tests
- Display words: **"Pregnant"** or **"Not Pregnant"**
- Some show **"Yes/No"** or **"+/-"** symbols

## Key Points About Positive Results

- **Even a faint line is positive** - it means hCG (pregnancy hormone) was detected
- A faint line often indicates early pregnancy when hormone levels are still low
- False positives are very rare

## Key Points About Negative Results

You may get a false negative if:
- You tested too early (before or right after a missed period)
- Your urine was too diluted (drank lots of fluids beforehand)
- The test was expired
- You didn't follow instructions correctly

## When to Test for Best Accuracy

| Timing | Accuracy |
|--------|----------|
| 4 days before missed period | ~50-60% |
| 2 days before missed period | ~80-90% |
| Day of missed period | 97-99% |
| 1 week after missed period | 99%+ |

**Best practice**: Use **first morning urine** for highest hCG concentration, especially when testing early.

## Important Time Window

- Read results within the specified time (usually **3-10 minutes**)
- Results after 10 minutes may not be valid
- An "evaporation line" can appear after the time window and be mistaken for a positive

## When to See a Doctor

- After any positive home test (to confirm and begin prenatal care)
- If you get multiple negative tests but your period is significantly late
- If you have unusual pain or bleeding with a positive test
- If results are confusing or inconsistent

## Factors That Can Affect Results

- **Fertility medications** containing hCG can cause false positives
- Certain medical conditions (rarely) can affect results
- Expired or improperly stored tests
- Not following instructions precisely
